newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CRICKET-BENJAMIN BOOST FOR WEST INDIES' SECOND TEST.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-BENJAMIN BOOST FOR WEST INDIES' SECOND TEST.

text.p: West Indies fast bowler Kenneth Benjamin passed a fitness test on Thursday to boost the tourists before the second test against Australia, starting on Friday.
Benjamin, rated a doubtful starter by captain Courtney Walsh two days ago, proved his recovery from a knee injury during a practice session.

Australia, who won the first test by 123 runs in Brisbane on Tuesday, have discarded wrist spinner Peter McIntyre from their original 13-man squad. Part-time spinners Michael Bevan and Mark Waugh are expected to support leg-spinner Shane Warne.
Australia have named all-rounder Greg Blewett as replacement for Steve Waugh, who injured his groin in the first test.
West Indies will delay naming their side until a final inspection of the Sydney Cricket Ground wicket before the start of play.
"Kenneth did not have any problem in the nets and did not complain about his knee. He is available for selection," Walsh told Reuters.
Walsh said he would be looking for a 20 to 30 percent improvement in all aspects of his side's performance following their heavy defeat in Brisbane.

The decision to leave out McIntyre means Australia will field three fast bowlers, with Jason Gillespie and Michael Kasprowicz competing for a place alongside new ball pair Glenn McGrath and Paul Reiffel.
Australia captain Mark Taylor said the balance of his side would be better served by leaving out McIntyre in favour of a third fast bowler.
"I think we need the extra quick in the 11 tomorrow compared to an extra spinner," Taylor said.

"I've got some options but if we go in with only two quicks and have to bowl on the first day we're a bit short in the fast bowling department," Taylor said, explaining the decision to cut McIntyre from the squad.
"The fact we've got Michael Bevan and Mark Waugh as back up for Shane Warne, if we played two quicks we've only got (medium pace bowler) Greg Blewett as support for them," he said.
Bevan proved an unexpected hero in Australia's first test win after he picked up three crucial second innings wickets with his left-arm wrist spin.
Mark Waugh offers Taylor a further bowling option with his makeshift off-spin.

Australia (from) - Mark Taylor (captain), Matthew Elliott, Ricky Ponting, Mark Waugh, Greg Blewett, Michael Bevan, Ian Healy, Shane Warne, Paul Reiffel, Glenn McGrath, Michael Kasprowicz, Jason Gillespie.

West Indies (from) - Sherwin Campbell, Robert Samuels, Brian Lara, Carl Hooper, Shivnarine Chanderpaul, Jimmy Adams, Courtney Browne, Ian Bishop, Curtly Ambrose, Courtney Walsh (captain), Kenneth Benjamin, Patterson Thompson, Adrian Griffith, Nixon McLean.
